newsitem.title: CHINA: China govt buys 3,000 T of domestic tungsten.
newsitem.headline: China govt buys 3,000 T of domestic tungsten.

text.p: The Chinese government has bought 3,000 tonnes of fine tungsten ore from state-owned mines that have cut production, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The official agency did not say what prices were paid or give details of when the purchases were made or from which mines they were obtained.
Metals officials said last week China was considering halting production at some state-owned tungsten mines to cut output and support falling world prices.
Lack of controls on output from some Chinese mines were seen as a major cause of prolonged pressure on tungsten prices, Xinhua said.

International tungsten producers at a conference in central Jiangxi province had called for producing nations to cut the extraction and sale of ore to boost prices, it said, adding that only a few countries had acted to limit output of ore.
"The Chinese government has taken the step of purchasing 3,000 tons of fine tungsten ore from state-owned mines which have reduced their production of tungsten," it said but did not elaborate.

China is the world's largest producer of tungsten, a metal used mainly to make carbide tools and special steel for the automobile and construction industries. Tungsten prices have been pressured due to oversupply.
